newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - APRIL 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - APRIL 23.

text.p: LIDOVE NOVINY - The Czech Republic's trade deficit for the first three months of this year was 40.2 billion crowns in comparison to 27.1 billion in 1996. March added 13.4 billion crowns to the deficit, less than the original estimate of 17 billion. Imports in the first quarter amounted to 188.2 billion crowns, exports to 148 billion, according to the Czech Statistical Bureau (CSU).
- The crown strengthened yesterday to 1.35 below parity, due to the results of the trade deficit announced in the morning, which were better than expected.

- On the last day of Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin's visit, an addition to the agreement for resolving Russia's debts to the Czech Republic was signed. Although payment of the debts has been put off for now, interest from Czech claims should be paid within three years.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik said yesterday that the current course of the crown, which is below parity, is positive, because it is something the cabinet's economic measures will definitely be helped by.
- The year-on-year increase in M2 money reached 8.4 percent this January, excluding the deposits from SPT Telecom, and 7.1 percent with SPT's deposits.
- The union of medical workers (LOK) in Motol Hospital announced their readiness to strike, valid from today. They are protesting against the dismissal of the leading heart surgeon Josef Dvorak.
- Skoda Plzen signed a $62 million contract yesterday with the Serbian company EPS to complete construction of the heating power plant Kolubara B in Serbia.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - All the bank accounts of the opposition Social Democrats are frozen because of unpaid taxes. The party's employees are beginning to feel it, because Komercni Banka blocked their salaries from last month.

- The cabinet's new measure to increase wages by only 7.3 percent could cause about 45,000 state employees to lose their jobs this year. If budgetary organisations laid off about five percent of their workers, the original increase in wages of 12.5 percent could be preserved.
- The cabinet decided on the privatisation of Jan Becher Karlovy Vary yesterday.

- Agriculture Minister Josef Lux, who wants six billion crowns from the government budget to support farmers in unfavourable conditions, did not succeed with his proposal in a meeting of economic ministers yesterday.
- Union Banka, which took over three banks last year and saved them from bankruptcy, is planning to continue its expansion. The bank now wants to enter Foresbank as a significant investor.
PRAVO - Justice Minister Vlasta Parkanova is ready to leave her post if anonymous attacks, which are affecting her work, do not stop.
- Trinecke Zelezarny's losses were twice as high as expected and reached 817.5 million crowns.
- So far, six small banks are participating in the central bank's consolidation programme. These are Banka Hana, Pragobanka, Foresbank, Zemska Banka, Universal Banka and Moravia Banka.

- The board of directors and the supervisory council of Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka (CSOB) proposes that the bank not pay dividends for 1996 but put all of CSOB's net profits for last year, 3.006 billion crowns, into reserves.
